scenario_stem:
Tarnmere Retail Group operates 6 supermarket stores across Country X and employs 240 staff. The group is opening a new store in Bramfield next spring and must hire 30 sales assistants before March. Last year, the HR team received 1,400 CVs for just 25 vacancies, and managers found that one-third of applicants omitted key details such as previous retail experience or weekend availability.

The HR manager wants to introduce a standard application form for the Bramfield campaign, arguing that every candidate would answer the same questions and shortlisting would be faster and fairer. The store general manager prefers keeping CVs, believing they reveal personality and written communication skills that a form cannot capture. Designing and printing the new form will cost $600, and two managers would spend about 2 days each on the changeover.

questions.question_text: Define 'application form'.
questions.model_answer: An application form is a document containing a standard set of questions that all applicants for a vacancy must complete. It asks for personal details, qualifications and employment history so the employer can compare candidates on equal terms. [2]

knowledge_max_2: Document containing standard/set questions completed by all applicants
Requests personal details, qualifications and employment history for comparison

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits to Tarnmere Retail Group of using an application form for the Bramfield campaign.
questions.model_answer: Benefit 1: Application forms contain standard questions, so every one of the 1,400 applicants answers the same way [k], making shortlisting for the 30 sales assistant posts in Bramfield faster and fairer for managers [app]. Benefit 2: Forms force every candidate to provide key details such as retail experience, which one-third of last year's CVs omitted [k], so the HR team avoids wasting time on incomplete applications for the Bramfield campaign [app]. [4]

knowledge_max_2: Standard questions mean all candidates answer identically
Ensures key information is supplied by every applicant
application_max_2: Shortlisting 1,400 applicants for 30 Bramfield posts becomes faster and fairer
Solves the problem that one-third of last year's CVs omitted key details such as retail experience

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages of using CVs for selecting sales assistants.
questions.model_answer: Advantage 1: A CV lets each applicant present their skills and experience in their own way [k], revealing personality and written communication skills [app], so managers can judge how well a candidate would represent Tarnmere Retail Group in busy stores [an]. Advantage 2: CVs are quick and inexpensive for applicants to create and send [k], helping the group attract a large pool such as the 1,400 candidates it received last year [app], which increases the chance of finding excellent sales assistants for Bramfield [an]. [6]

knowledge_max_2: CV allows applicants to present skills and experience in their own format
CVs are quick and cheap for applicants to produce and send
application_max_2: Reveals personality and written communication skills the store general manager values

analysis_max_2: Better judgement of fit for customer-facing supermarket stores
Wider applicant pool raises the likelihood of appointing strong sales assistants for Bramfield

questions.question_text: Do you think Tarnmere Retail Group should introduce the application form for the Bramfield campaign? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Tarnmere Retail Group should introduce the application form because the 1,400 applicants would all answer identical questions [k], allowing two managers to shortlist the 30 sales assistants quickly and fairly, with about 2 days each on design a small one-off effort for the group [app]. This would also solve the problem of one-third of CVs omitting key details such as retail experience [an]. However, the store general manager prefers CVs because they reveal personality and written communication skills [k], which matter when staff speak to shoppers all day in 6 supermarket stores [app], and losing that insight could mean appointing assistants who perform poorly with customers and need replacing [an]. Overall, on balance the group should adopt the application form for the Bramfield campaign because consistency and speed at a scale of 1,400 applicants outweigh the extra insight CVs give for entry-level sales roles, with communication skills still checked at interview [eval]. The $600 cost is trivial compared with the wages and disruption of a poor appointment across 6 supermarket stores [eval].

evaluation_max_2: Balanced judgement that consistency wins at 1,400-applicant scale

scenario_stem:
Voss Engineering Ltd manufactures hydraulic pumps for agricultural machinery and employs 85 production staff at its plant in Dunwick. The company needs to hire 6 graduate production engineers to support four automated production lines, and has shortlisted 18 candidates from 320 applications received this year. The HR director believes practical aptitude tests would show which candidates can read engineering drawings and solve numerical problems before interviews are held.

The production manager argues that aptitude tests cost $1,800 to administer and take half a day to run, whereas one-to-one interviews cost almost nothing and reveal motivation and teamwork. The managing director must decide whether to test the 18 candidates or simply interview them and appoint the 6 best-performing interviewees within three weeks.

questions.question_text: Define 'aptitude test'.
questions.model_answer: An aptitude test is a selection method that measures a candidate's natural ability to carry out specific tasks, such as numerical reasoning or reading technical drawings. Employers use the results to predict how well a candidate can learn and perform the duties of the job. [2]

knowledge_max_2: Selection method measuring natural ability for specific tasks
Used to predict how well a candidate can learn and perform the job

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits of using aptitude tests for the graduate engineer recruitment.
questions.model_answer: Benefit 1: Aptitude tests give objective, measurable scores, so all 18 shortlisted candidates are assessed against the same practical tasks [k], helping the HR director identify which candidates can read engineering drawings and solve numerical problems for the 6 graduate engineer roles [app]. Benefit 2: Testing before interviewing filters out unsuitable candidates early [k], so the company avoids wasting interview time and fills the 6 posts within three weeks [app]. [4]

knowledge_max_2: Objective and measurable scores for every candidate
Filters out unsuitable candidates before interview
application_max_2: Checks ability to read engineering drawings and solve numerical problems
Supports appointing 6 graduate engineers within three weeks

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages of one-to-one interviews as a selection method for Voss Engineering Ltd.
questions.model_answer: Advantage 1: One-to-one interviews let the panel explore each candidate's motivation and teamwork [k], revealing qualities that the $1,800 aptitude tests cannot measure [app], so the production manager can judge whether a graduate fits the working culture at the Dunwick plant [an]. Advantage 2: Interviews are inexpensive to set up and run [k], which matters when filling 6 posts from a shortlist of 18 candidates [app], helping Voss Engineering Ltd control recruitment costs while assessing every candidate properly [an]. [6]

knowledge_max_2: Explores motivation and teamwork in depth
Inexpensive to set up and run
application_max_2: Reveals qualities tests cannot measure, such as motivation and teamwork
Low cost suited to filling 6 posts from 18 candidates
analysis_max_2: Better judgement of cultural fit at the Dunwick plant
Controls recruitment costs for a small engineering firm

questions.question_text: Do you think Voss Engineering Ltd should use aptitude tests before interviewing the 18 candidates? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Voss Engineering Ltd should use aptitude tests because they produce objective scores for all 18 candidates [k], allowing the HR director to check who can actually read engineering drawings and solve numerical problems rather than relying on interview impressions alone [app]. With 320 applications and only 6 graduate engineer roles, an evidence-based shortlist reduces the risk of a costly mis-hire in a technical manufacturing environment [an]. However, the production manager argues that one-to-one interviews cost almost nothing and reveal motivation and teamwork [k], which matters when engineers will work alongside 85 production staff at the Dunwick plant [app], so relying on tests alone could appoint technically strong but difficult colleagues [an]. Overall, on balance the company should use tests and then interview, because the $1,800 cost (about $100 per candidate) is small against the price of a wrong technical hire, and tests give the objective base the interviews lack [eval]. Both methods together give the most reliable route to appointing the right 6 engineers within three weeks [eval].

knowledge_max_2: Aptitude tests produce objective, measurable scores

application_max_2: Checks ability to read engineering drawings and solve numerical problems across 18 candidates
Cuts the field from 320 applications to 6 hires
analysis_max_2: Reduces risk of costly mis-hire in a technical environment
Test-only approach may miss motivation and teamwork fit
evaluation_max_2: Weighs $1,800 cost ($100 per candidate) against cost of a wrong hire
Concludes a combined tests-then-interviews approach is best

scenario_stem:
Caldermere Hotel Group runs 4 hotels in Country X and employs 320 staff. Its events coordinator at the Seacrest Grand Hotel resigned last month, leaving a vacancy earning $42,000 a year. The group has two strong internal candidates: Priya Nair, a banquet supervisor with 6 years of service, and Daniel Reyes, a conference sales team leader with 4 years of service.

Alternatively, the HR director could advertise externally and attract experienced events professionals from outside the group, at an estimated recruitment cost of $9,500 including advertising and agency fees. External advertising would take around 4 weeks and could attract 30 or more applicants. The chief executive must decide whether to promote internally or recruit from outside; whichever route is chosen, the post must be filled before the peak wedding season in June.

questions.question_text: Define 'internal recruitment'.
questions.model_answer: Internal recruitment is filling a vacancy by appointing someone who already works for the business, for example through promotion or transfer, rather than hiring from outside the organisation. [2]

knowledge_max_2: Filling a vacancy with an existing employee
Includes promotion or transfer from within the business

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages of recruiting the events coordinator internally.
questions.model_answer: Advantage 1: Internal candidates are already known to the group, so managers have direct evidence of their performance and reliability [k], meaning Priya Nair or Daniel Reyes' work as banquet supervisor and conference sales team leader is proven rather than untested [app]. Advantage 2: Filling the vacancy internally is quicker and cheaper [k], avoiding the estimated $9,500 cost of advertising and agency fees and allowing the post to be filled before the June wedding season [app]. [4]

knowledge_max_2: Internal candidates are already known and tested in the business
Quicker and cheaper than external recruitment
application_max_2: Proven records of Priya Nair (6 years) and Daniel Reyes (4 years)

Advantage 2: An external hire brings fresh ideas and avoids internal rivalries [k], which matters if Priya Nair and Daniel Reyes both applied and one is appointed over the other [app], helping the events team work smoothly in the run-up to the June wedding season [an]. questions.question_text: Do you think Caldermere Hotel Group should recruit the events coordinator internally or externally? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Caldermere Hotel Group should prioritise internal recruitment because Priya Nair and Daniel Reyes are proven performers whose work is already known across the 4 hotels [k], so appointing either avoids the $9,500 cost of external advertising and agency fees [app]. Filling the post quickly from within also protects service during the June wedding season, when occupancy peaks [an]. However, internal recruitment means one strong candidate may feel passed over [k], risking lower morale or even resignation in a hotel employing 320 staff [app], whereas an external hire would add fresh expertise but at extra cost and with a 4-week advertising timeline that could delay the appointment until after the June peak [an]. Overall, on balance the group should promote internally, choosing the stronger candidate on merit, because the cost saving, speed and known track records outweigh the modest benefit of outside experience for a coordinator post [eval]. scenario_stem:
Hathersage Garden Centre employs 18 staff in a rural location and is busiest at weekends and during the spring planting season, when customer numbers double. The owner wants to replace 4 full-time checkout employees who resigned, but weekend trade now generates 60% of weekly revenue and weekday mornings are quiet, with fewer than 50 customers by noon. The planting season typically begins in February and lasts until early May when the weather is favourable.

The owner is considering recruiting 8 part-time employees working Saturday, Sunday and Wednesday shifts instead of 4 full-time replacements. Full-time replacements would have cost $108,000 a year, so part-time staff at $11.50 per hour would save an estimated $12,000 a year, but full-time staff would offer more consistent service and need less supervision and training overall.

questions.question_text: Define 'part-time employee'.
questions.model_answer: A part-time employee is a worker contracted for fewer hours per week than a full-time employee, for example weekend or reduced weekday shifts. Pay and benefits are usually calculated pro rata against full-time staff. [2]

knowledge_max_2: Works fewer hours per week than a full-time employee

Benefit 2: Part-time employees at $11.50 per hour cost less than full-time replacements [k], saving an estimated $12,000 a year against the $108,000 full-time bill [app]. [4]

questions.model_answer: Drawback 1: Replacing 4 full-time employees with 8 part-time workers doubles the number of people to train and supervise [k], increasing the workload for the owner of an 18-staff business [app], so induction and supervision costs could erode the projected $12,000 annual saving [an]. Drawback 2: Part-time staff often lack the product knowledge of full-time workers [k], so service quality during the spring planting season could slip [app], risking the garden centre's reputation and repeat custom [an]. questions.model_answer: Hathersage Garden Centre should recruit the part-time employees because they can be concentrated on the weekend trade that generates 60% of weekly revenue [k], letting the centre serve doubled customer numbers without paying for idle hours on quiet weekday mornings [app]. scenario_stem:
Quillfern Software Ltd employs 55 developers and analysts creating accounting packages for small businesses in Country X. The company has grown by 25% in two years and now serves 40 small business clients. It now wants to hire 5 graduate analysts to support this growth and has shortlisted 20 candidates. The HR manager has proposed a half-day assessment centre with group exercises, a presentation and an in-tray task, costing $3,000 in total.

The technical director argues that a structured 45-minute panel interview is cheaper at $400 in total and enough to judge each candidate, while the HR manager believes behaviour and teamwork shown at an assessment centre better predict job performance. The board must decide which method to use before offers are made in September.

questions.question_text: Define 'assessment centre'.
questions.model_answer: An assessment centre is a selection method in which candidates complete a series of tasks and exercises, such as group discussions, presentations and problem-solving activities, while trained assessors observe and score their performance. [2]

knowledge_max_2: Candidates complete a series of tasks and exercises
Assessors observe and score performance across the activities

Benefit 2: Group exercises reveal teamwork and communication skills [k], which Quillfern Software Ltd needs in graduate analysts supporting 40 small business clients [app]. [4]

knowledge_max_2: Multiple exercises show behaviour over a longer period
Reveals teamwork and communication skills
application_max_2: Richer comparison across 20 shortlisted candidates
Matches the needs of analysts supporting 40 small business clients

questions.model_answer: Advantage 1: A 45-minute panel interview costs only $400 in total [k], compared with $3,000 for the assessment centre [app], so the company spends far less at a time when the 55-person business is investing in growth [an]. Advantage 2: Panel interviews are quicker to arrange and give each candidate direct time to discuss motivation and career goals [k], helping the technical director judge commitment to the analyst role [app], which speeds up offers before the September start [an]. [6]

questions.question_text: Do you think Quillfern Software Ltd should run the assessment centre rather than rely on panel interviews for the 5 graduate analyst roles? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Quillfern Software Ltd should run the assessment centre because exercises such as group tasks, a presentation and an in-tray activity reveal how all 20 candidates actually behave [k], not just how they answer questions in a 45-minute interview [app]. For 5 graduate analysts supporting 40 small business clients, seeing teamwork and problem-solving in practice reduces the risk of an expensive mis-hire [an]. However, the technical director is right that $3,000 is much more than $400 [k], and a poorly organised assessment centre can feel repetitive or intimidating to able candidates [app], causing them to withdraw and accept offers elsewhere at a time of 25% growth [an]. Overall, on balance the company should hold the assessment centre, because at $150 per candidate the extra $2,600 is modest against the cost of a wrong appointment, and structured interviews can still be kept within the day [eval]. This combined approach best predicts which 5 candidates will succeed with small business clients before the September start [eval].

analysis_max_2: Better prediction of on-the-job performance for analysts

evaluation_max_2: Weighs $150 per candidate against cost of a mis-hire
Concludes assessment centre plus interviews is the best route

scenario_stem:

scenario_stem:
Brackmere City Council employs 1,150 staff delivering waste collection, leisure centres and social care in Country X. The council uses a standard application form for all vacancies and received 260 applications for 8 administrative officer posts last year. Councillors have asked whether the council should accept CVs instead, arguing the form is outdated and discourages younger applicants from applying.

The form guarantees every candidate supplies the same information, supporting fair, consistent shortlisting and the council's equal opportunities policy. Moving to CVs could modernise recruitment, but officers estimate rewriting the process would cost $4,500 and take 3 months, and 90% of councils in comparable regions still use application forms for consistency and legal defensibility. The form is also translated into 2 community languages.

scenario_stem:
Yewbank Electronics Ltd assembles small household appliances and employs 130 workers in Country X. A production line leader resigned and must be replaced. The HR manager has shortlisted 2 internal candidates after interviews: Tomas Silva, a team leader of 4 years earning $29,000, and Aisha Rahman, a quality inspector of 7 years earning $31,000.

A practical problem-solving assessment is scheduled next week, costing $500. The production director believes the assessment will reveal which candidate can handle real line faults and calm staff under pressure, while the HR manager warns that the cost of choosing wrongly is high: the last mis-hire disrupted output worth $85,000 before being replaced after 5 months. The managing director must decide whether to rely on interviews alone or add the assessment.
